summary: [P2] Audit: Cloning a webhook response without consuming both branches lets a receiver stall delivery in acmeclose-openfaas (up to Medium)
description:
Current reporting scale: Medium = P3 = Medium.

Blocker = P0 = Severe; Critical = P1 = Critical; Major = P2 = High; Medium = P3 = Medium; Minor = P4 = Low.

This five-level scale supersedes the earlier P0-P3 mapping. The audit text below retains its original severity and priority wording as historical evidence.

Original title: [P2] Audit: Cloning a webhook response without consuming both branches lets a receiver stall delivery in acmeclose-openfaas (Medium)

Problem and impact

Cloning a webhook response without consuming both branches lets a receiver stall delivery

A webhook receiver controls the response body to a delivery request. After node-fetch returns a successful response, the code creates a clone and consumes only the clone with text(); the original response branch is never read. In node-fetch 2.x, cloned Node streams must be consumed in parallel because an unread branch applies backpressure once its small stream buffer fills. A receiver can therefore return a 2xx body larger than that buffer and hold the invocation before archival. Repeated deliveries occupy worker capacity and build queue lag without requiring an error status.

Attacker access and control

The attacker must control or compromise a webhook receiver selected by an accepted payload, then cause or wait for a delivery to that receiver. The attacker controls the status and response byte length and can return a finite body under a 2xx status.

Attack path

When the worker sends the outbound request, return HTTP 200 with a body larger than node-fetch's clone stream buffer. sendRequest accepts the 2xx response. processPayload calls response.clone().text() but never consumes response.body, so backpressure from the unread original branch prevents the clone from completing. The handler never reaches the archive move or success callback until a surrounding timeout or process termination releases it; repeating the response consumes concurrent worker slots and delays other webhooks.

Why current controls do not stop it

The Express 100 KB request-body limit applies only to inbound invocation JSON. The HTTP timeout can eventually release an affected request, but each attacker response can still occupy the invocation for that window, and the code defines no total job concurrency or response-byte bound. Rejecting non-2xx responses is irrelevant because the receiver uses 2xx.

What to change

Do not clone the response. Consume response.text() once, apply an explicit byte limit, and reuse that bounded string for logging and legacy XML validation. If two consumers are required, start both response branches in parallel as required by node-fetch 2.x. Also log only a bounded redacted excerpt or correlation identifier.

How to verify safely

In an isolated harness using the committed node-fetch 2.x resolution, have a local receiver return HTTP 200 with a finite body larger than the clone stream high-water mark. Call the outbound path with fabricated data and use a short harness deadline. Verify that clone().text() does not complete while the original response branch remains unread. Do not use a production receiver or queue.

Assumptions

• 
At least one accepted webhook destination can be controlled or compromised by an attacker and remains reachable from the worker.

• 
The deployed dependency remains on the node-fetch 2.x line required by the committed function manifest and retains its documented clone stream behavior.

• 
No transparent proxy outside this repository rejects the response before it exceeds the clone stream buffer.


Evidence

• 
utils/http.js:7-27
: The outbound helper passes a timeout but no response-size option to node-fetch and returns every successful response for later consumption.

• 
utils/request-processor.js:129-150
: Every successful webhook response is cloned and only the clone is converted to text; the original response body is never consumed before logging or XML parsing.

• 
webhook-delivery/package.json:17-23
: The webhook function directly depends on the CommonJS node-fetch 2.x line whose cloned Node streams require parallel consumption.

• 
yarn.lock:2798-2800
: The committed root lock resolves the CommonJS node-fetch dependency used by the helper to the reviewed 2.x implementation.

None identified from committed source.

comments.body:
[agent] Kickoff research (read-only, main as of 2026-10-08)

Finding verified?
 Yes. 
utils/request-processor.js:140
 calls 
response.clone().text()
 and never consumes the original body. node-fetch resolves to 2.6.7 (
yarn.lock:2798-2800
), where clone pipes one source into two PassThroughs. Once the unread branch's buffer fills, it applies backpressure and the clone read stalls. The stall is bounded: node-fetch 2.x applies the 
timeout
 option (60s default, 
utils/http.js:12,20
) to body reads too. A large 2xx body therefore stalls for about 60s and then throws a body-timeout. The side effect is worse than a stall: a delivery the receiver already accepted is treated as failed (424), then retried/DLQ'd, which can cause duplicate sends.

Fix approach

• 
Replace 
response.clone().text()
 with a single bounded read. Use node-fetch's 
size
 option in 
sendRequest
, or read the stream with a byte cap, and reuse the string for logging and XML parsing.

• 
Log a truncated or redacted excerpt rather than the full 
resp
 (
:141-146
). This partly covers threat model SKL-07.

• 
Decide what to do when the response exceeds the cap. Recommended: treat it as success for JSON payload types, since the 2xx is already received, and fail for SOFTPRO_LEGACY_XML, which needs the body.


LOE
: Trivial. 1 small PR in acmeclose-openfaas and a webhook-delivery redeploy. No infra, no secrets, no other teams. Low regression risk. Only the legacy XML success parse depends on the body.

Kickoff pointers
: 
processPayload
 in 
utils/request-processor.js
, 
sendRequest
 in 
utils/http.js
. Add a mocked test with a local http server returning a large 200 body; the existing 
__tests__/request-processor.js
 hits live AWS/httpbin, so add a separate mocked suite. Dependabot PR #1 (open) bumps deps; check it doesn't move node-fetch major. Related: SK-2823.

main-ab5a6d3

. 
Not confirmed deployed anywhere yet.
 Before testing, check bay-deployments for a commit "set image tag main-2824789" and that the ArgoCD app shows image

 and Synced/Healthy. If the pipeline did not run, ask the Bay/DevOps on-call to re-trigger it.

• 
Access: AWS 
acme-dev
 profile (integ account 000000000000) via Granted (see the 
aws-profiles
 skill); Grafana NPE (Loki); an integ Bay user; optionally ArgoCD read access.


2. Setup

• 
Receiver: use webhook.site or a local server behind ngrok (the function runs in-cluster, so the URL must be internet-reachable). Prepare responses: (a) 200 with a short JSON body, (b) 200 with a body > 64 KB (e.g. 100 KB of 
x
), (c) 200 with 
<xml><success>true</success></xml>
, (d) 200 with 
<xml><success>false</success></xml>
.

• 
Trigger: use 
webhook-traffic-generator/
 (run 
yarn install
 there). Edit 
index.js
 locally: set 
ENDPOINT_URL
 to your receiver; for the XML cases also delete the 
payloadType: "JSON"
 line in 
payload.js
 so the function falls back to 
SOFTPRO_LEGACY_XML
. Run 
AWS_PROFILE=acme-dev AWS_REGION=us-west-2 node index.js
, then 
curl -X POST localhost:8080/send
 once per case. It writes an encrypted object to bucket 
acmeclose-webhook-delivery-integ
 under 
queue/
 using KMS alias 
acmeclose-webhook-payload-encryption-key-integ
. Do not revert these edits into a commit.

• 
Why not the UI: acmeclose-api only emits 
JSON
 integrator webhooks (
IntegratorWebhookResponseType
 has a single value), so the XML path and a > 64 KB response cannot be produced from Bay. Creating a package in integ does fire a real Bearer-auth JSON webhook to Bay's own API, which is the regression check in step 5.


3. Test cases

• 
TC1 small 200 JSON: delivered once, object moves to 
history/
.

• 
TC2 200 with > 64 KB body (previously stalled 60s, returned 424, retried): completes in seconds, no retry, moves to 
history/
.

• 
TC3 XML 
<success>true</success>
 (large body ok): success, moves to 
history/
.

• 
TC4 XML 
<success>false</success>
 with a padded body: function fails 424, SQS retries, then DLQ function moves it to 
dlq/
 and posts a Slack "Webhook Undeliverable" alert.


4. Verification

• 
Logs: Grafana NPE, Loki datasource 
grafanacloud-logs
, query 
{namespace="integ-bay", app="acmeclose-webhook-delivery"} |= "<filename>.json"
. The info line must have 
code
, 
resp
 (at most 256 chars, ending in 
…
 when truncated), 
responseBytes
 equal to the real body size, and must NOT contain the full body. For TC4 the error line's 
returned bad response:
 text is the 256-char excerpt only. DLQ logs: 
app="acmeclose-webhook-delivery-dlq"
.

• 
S3: 
aws s3 ls s3://acmeclose-webhook-delivery-integ/history/
 (or 
dlq/
) for your filename; 
queue/
 should be empty of it.

• 
Receiver shows exactly one POST per case (TC4 shows the retries).


5. Regression

• 
In integ Bay, create a disclosure package: this exercises the Bearer (
http.getToken
) + JSON path end to end; expect 
code: 204
 in the log. Basic/None auth and the mocked large-body cases are covered by 
yarn jest __tests__/request-processor.unit.js
 (no AWS needed). 
__tests__/request-processor.js
 hits live AWS/httpbin and is optional.


6. Rollback

• 
Revert the integ image tag commit in bay-deployments (set 
.acme-func.image.tag
 back to 
main-ab5a6d3
); ArgoCD auto-syncs. Prod is untouched until a tag is cut.


Not confirmed
: pipeline run status for 
2824789f
; whether 
webhook-traffic-generator
 still installs cleanly (aws-sdk v2 pinned); the exact SQS retry count before DLQ.

pull_requests.title: SK-2826 fix(webhook-delivery): bound receiver response excerpt in logs and errors
pull_requests.github_description:
Every delivery logged the full receiver response body, and the bad-XML-response error embedded it too. Receivers often echo the webhook payload, which carries transaction and customer data, and a hostile receiver could inflate log volume without limit. The log entry now carries a 256-character excerpt (with an ellipsis marker when truncated) plus responseBytes, and the thrown error uses the same excerpt; XML success parsing still uses the full body.

Stacked on #5.

https://acme.atlassian.net/browse/SK-2826

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Observability-only change that reduces PII/log volume; delivery and XML validation behavior on the full body are unchanged.
> 
> **Overview**
> Webhook delivery no longer writes the full receiver response into logs or failure messages. **`processPayload`** now logs a **256-character excerpt** (with an ellipsis when truncated), adds **`responseBytes`** for the full body size, and uses the same excerpt in the **SOFTPRO_LEGACY_XML** “bad response” error. XML success parsing still reads the complete response body.
> 
> Unit tests cover truncation, byte-length accounting (including multi-byte characters), short bodies, preserved log fields (`verb`, `url`, `code`), and that oversized failure payloads are not embedded in error text.

pull_requests.title: SK-2826 fix(webhook-delivery): large webhook responses stall on unread clone() branch
pull_requests.github_description:
processPayload read the webhook response body only from response.clone(). node-fetch 2.x tees the body on clone, so the untouched original branch backs up once its buffer fills and any response larger than roughly 16 KB stalled until the 60s timeout. A delivery the receiver had already accepted was then marked failed and retried. The response is never used after the body is read, so this reads response.text() directly, and adds an offline regression test (mocked responses plus a real node-fetch Response streaming a large body).

The size-cap and bounded log-excerpt suggestions from the Audit finding are intentionally left for a follow-up.

https://acme.atlassian.net/browse/SK-2826

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches core webhook delivery and response logging/parsing; behavior change is narrow but affects production delivery outcomes for large receiver responses.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes webhook deliveries that **stall and time out** when receivers return response bodies larger than ~16 KB. `processPayload` now reads the HTTP response with **`response.text()`** instead of **`response.clone().text()`**, avoiding node-fetch 2.x’s tee’d body where an unread clone branch fills its buffer and blocks until the 60s timeout—causing accepted deliveries to be marked failed and retried.
> 
> Adds **`processPayload`** export for testing and a new unit suite covering large JSON/XML success paths (asserting **no `clone()`**), a streaming **node-fetch `Response`**, and unchanged **SOFTPRO_LEGACY_XML** failure handling.
>

repo_files.webhook-delivery/Dockerfile:
FROM node:16-alpine

RUN apk --no-cache add curl ca-certificates tini \
    && addgroup -S app && adduser -S -g app app

ENV NPM_CONFIG_LOGLEVEL=warn

# Cap V8's old-space heap so it stays inside the container memory limit.
# Pair this with a deployment memory limit of >= 256Mi.
ENV NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=192"

RUN chmod 777 /tmp

USER app

WORKDIR /home/app

# Copy and install dependencies
COPY webhook-delivery/package.json ./
RUN npm i

# Copy application wrapper and instrumentation
COPY webhook-delivery/index.js webhook-delivery/instrumentation.js ./

# Copy function handler
COPY webhook-delivery/handler.js ./

# Copy shared utilities
COPY utils/ ./utils/

# Run tests
RUN npm test

EXPOSE 8080

ENTRYPOINT ["tini", "--"]
CMD ["node", "--require", "./instrumentation.js", "index.js"]
